Why should you pay for two Seats in an Aircraft

For the purpose of this post, I'm going to refrain, as much as I can, from the circlejerk that is the fph hate machine, and go into, from a safety standpoint, why “Persons of Size” need to pay for two seats.

Quick Background on me, without doxxing myself, I have 1400+hrs flying, was a baggage handler, and a cargomaster, so in my own opinion, I'm qualified to give a quick post on this subject.

NOTE: ALL WEIGHTS ARE IN POUNDS, BUT THIS IS FOR CANADA, YMMV

Standard weights for males above 12 years old are 200lbs, and 206 pounds in winter – presumably because your winter gear weighs more than your pair of jeans and tshirt does.

Standard weights for females above 12 years old are 165lbs, and 171lbs – same seasonal qualifiers as above, children are 75lbs year round.

Now that you have the numbers, onto the safety aspect.

I don't remember the the exact 727 loading envelope, but iirc, it was about 8”. To give you an idea of what this 'loading envelope' is, take a see-saw (teetertotter?) - the fulcrim point is the 'envelope' in this case. Too much weight in the nose, the aircraft does not get off the ground, too much weight in the back end, she can't pitch forward, tailstall/tail slides, plummets to the ground, and bursts into bits for the TC/NTSB/(YOUR INVESTIGATIVE BODY OF CHOICE HERE) pick up.

Now, I hear you say “But DerpyDoom, I don't fly on a 727. That has no relevance to me.” Ahah. But it does, so sit back, and listen up, because here's why.

A Boeing 737NG-7/800 has a 10” envelope. There are things the Captain can do to extend that, but only to a point. (I think it was up to 12” (For those of you keeping score at home, that's a total of 6” front or back of the desired point)).

“Damnit Derpy, get to the point!” I hear you cry, well, fine.

Average aircraft holds 143 people. Based on weights above, no one “over” those? That's cool. Front half under that and back half at those weights? Possible Tail stall. Nose WAY over that, and tail under that? Have fun with your fiery death.

Weight takes fuel to move. Put in too little, you divert or worse. Fuel Weighs as well, most airlines don't like 'tankering' unless they have to, because it costs money to move weight.

Semi-related – if the aircraft goes down somewhere, and the 'Person of Size' can't get out, or worse, impedes others, or can't get out of the emergency exit over the window due to a water landing, and kills everyone on board...

Tl;dr Wings can only supply so much lift, and you need to pull your head from your ass and not be offended over safety concerns.
